answer.rationale: The two observed declines are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), which points directly at the funnel rather than at price. Two inherited memories (86, 31) independently support onboarding/signup simplification producing durable activation lift, so I verify exactly those two: memory_31 is the oldest (day 12) and claims a 'durable' lift that may not have been measured long enough, and memory_86 is a day-52 consolidation whose underlying record may overlap with memory_31 rather than being independent evidence 	he apparent corroboration could be one experiment counted twice. Confirming independence and durability is the highest-value use of scarce analyst time. I deliberately do not spend budget on memory_73 (promotional pricing) because its record already carries the decisive detail: a 40% discount bought a 31% activation gain and 18% revenue gain but cost 12 points of renewal retention. That is precisely the trap the competitor's entry pricing invites us into, and it directly contradicts the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue \u2014 short-term activation purchased with downstream churn. Referral incentives (57) worked in established customers, which is not where the current damage is; enterprise sales-assist (44) is sound but does not address SMB funnel decay. Activation messaging (91) is the strong runner-up and would be my fallback if verification shows 86 and 31 are the same experiment or that the lift decayed. I am running a standard experiment rather than a broad rollout because the funnel decline is recent and its cause is not yet established \u2014 the drop may be competitor-driven demand-mix shift rather than genuine onboarding regression, in which case simplification will underperform its historical numbers. I flag downstream value risk: reducing signup friction can admit lower-intent accounts that activate but never become qualified revenue, so success must be measured on retained qualified revenue at renewal, not on activation counts alone \u2014 the same metric that would have caught the memory_73 failure.
